incidents.summary: The World Health Organization's director-general stated that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading faster than response efforts can contain, as aid workers continue to strike over unpaid wages. A Reuters explainer highlighted factors driving the rapid spread, including conflict, community mistrust, and a lack of approved treatments or vaccines for the Bundibugyo strain. These developments underscore the ongoing challenges in containing the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record.

logs.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the fastest-growing ever, with cases surging above 1,000 and the death toll reaching 600. The outbreak has spread to new provinces including Tshopo and Haut-Uele, and the first case outside Africa has been confirmed in France. Response efforts are hampered by funding shortages, unpaid health workers, and the closure of USAID, while new diagnostic tests and treatment trials offer hope.

news.headline: Médecins Sans Frontières Launches 'Keep Life Breathing' Roving Exhibition to Spotlight Humanitarian Crises and Ebola Disease Outbreak in DRC
news.body: HONG KONG, July 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) Hong Kong yesterday held an opening ceremony for its 'Keep Life Breathing' Roving Exhibition. As a key part of its annual 'MSF Day' campaign, the exhibition will tour three locations throughout July: The Wai, Festival Walk, and TKO Plaza. It showcases real-life stories of MSF providing emergency medical humanitarian assistance to people affected by protracted conflicts and crises. The event also features an Ebola disease-themed zone, which aims to deepen public awareness and understanding of the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

logs.summary: On August 3, 2026, severe thunderstorms and heavy rain brought flash flood warnings to New York City, New Jersey, Central Jersey, and southeastern Pennsylvania, with rainfall rates of 1–3 inches per hour and localized totals up to 5 inches possible. Flood watches remained in effect across the Mid-Atlantic, and Charlotte, North Carolina, also faced increased severe weather potential. Meanwhile, in Wisconsin's Fox Cities, recovery efforts continued a week after storms, with over 8,200 meals served and road closures set.

logs.summary: Recent reports show continued severe thunderstorm and flash flood threats across the central and eastern U.S., with forecasts for strong storms and heavy downpours over the weekend. Monday night severe weather diverted 22 flights from Denver to Colorado Springs, while separate storms triggered severe thunderstorm and flash flood warnings in northern Arizona and damaging wind/hail warnings in New York's Capital Region, Hudson Valley, and Southern Tier. Power outages were reported in the Midlands, and severe weather also forced the Kansas City Chiefs to practice indoors and prompted strong storm alerts in Wisconsin.

logs.summary: On August 7, 2026, severe thunderstorms prompted watches and warnings from the National Weather Service across Delaware, New York (including Hudson Valley, Broome, and Sullivan counties), and surrounding states. Over 40,000 New Jersey residents lost power as storms rolled through, while quarter-sized hail and damaging winds affected multiple counties, and lightning caused a weather delay at Nissan Stadium in Tennessee. A Next Weather Alert was in effect for the Philadelphia region due to the combination of heat and heavy storms.

The earthquake was located near the Hicks Bay area, consistent with the reported incident. No additional details about damage or tsunami warnings were provided in the news excerpts.
